# Just Ask the Model: One-Shot LLM Research Evaluation and Structured Expert Review

> A working paper comparing structured one-shot research evaluations by GPT-5 Pro with paid expert review packages from The Unjournal, on percentile ratings and narrative critiques of economics and social-science working papers.

Authors: Valentin Klotzbücher (University of Basel & University Hospital Basel), David Reinstein (The Unjournal), Lorenzo Pacchiardi (University of Cambridge, Leverhulme Centre for the Future of Intelligence), Tianmai Michael Zhang (University of Washington).

A collaboration with The Unjournal (https://www.unjournal.org/), an open evaluation platform for economics and social-science research. Code and data: https://github.com/valentinklotzbuecher/llm-uj-research-eval

## Summary

Humans and GPT-5 Pro rate the same papers on seven percentile criteria, with uncertainty intervals, and write narrative critiques. Treating the human evaluations as a high-quality but noisy reference signal, GPT-5 Pro approaches the agreement levels seen among human evaluators on several criteria. It also shows consistent failure modes: compressed rating scales, uneven coverage of criteria, and variable identification of the concerns experts flagged. The setup is deliberately minimal: one prompt with a fixed rubric, no iteration or retrieval. Uncertainty in the human benchmark, and the assumptions behind the reliability adjustment, rule out a claim that the model is equivalent to an additional expert. Appendices cover five further models with differing sample coverage and an exploratory comparison of the issues raised by the model and by experts.

## Paper

- [Introduction](https://llm-uj-research-eval.netlify.app/): motivation, research question, and summary of findings
- [Results](https://llm-uj-research-eval.netlify.app/results.html): rating agreement between GPT-5 Pro and the human panel, and whether the model finds the issues experts find
- [Discussion](https://llm-uj-research-eval.netlify.app/discussion.html)
- [Methods](https://llm-uj-research-eval.netlify.app/methods.html): data, prompt, rubric, and evaluation pipeline
- [Headless Codex Pilot](https://llm-uj-research-eval.netlify.app/headless_codex_pilot.html): exploratory extension, kept separate from the main API-based evidence
- [References](https://llm-uj-research-eval.netlify.app/references.html)
- [PDF version](https://llm-uj-research-eval.netlify.app/Just-Ask-the-Model--One-Shot-LLM-Research-Evaluation-and-Structured-Expert-Review.pdf)

## Appendices

- [Appendix A: Results: Ratings](https://llm-uj-research-eval.netlify.app/results_ratings.html): rating comparisons across all models
- [Appendix B: Results: Critiques & Key Issues](https://llm-uj-research-eval.netlify.app/results_critiques.html): paper-by-paper comparison of the issues raised by the model and by human evaluators
- [Appendix C: Supplementary Material](https://llm-uj-research-eval.netlify.app/appendix_llm_traces.html): extended rating and critique analysis
- [Appendix D: Did Authors Respond to Unjournal Evaluations?](https://llm-uj-research-eval.netlify.app/paper_response_analysis.html): evidence on whether papers changed after evaluation
